steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: A searching algorithm finds the position of a specific item (the target) within a data structure such as a list or array. If the item is found, the algorithm returns its position; if not, it indicates the item is not present. | Linear search: checks each item in the list sequentially, starting from the first element, until the target is found or the end of the list is reached. It works on both sorted and unsorted data. | Binary search: works on a sorted list . It compares the target with the middle element. If the target is smaller, the search continues in the left half. If larger, it continues in the right half.
